tasks.title: Define the two clause strings
tasks.acceptance: Two unexported constants hold §2.2's and §3.2's strings byte-for-byte as the fenced blocks give them. A test asserts each against the literal.

tasks.title: Build the 468-byte suffix
tasks.acceptance: One helper returns LF LF + clause A + LF LF + clause B. A test asserts its length is exactly 468.

tasks.title: Append the suffix to role prompts
tasks.acceptance: In tp review's and tp audit's prompt assembly, a prompt whose output_path is non-empty has its trailing newline removed then the suffix appended. A prompt whose output_path is empty is left untouched.

tasks.title: Relocate review state for tests
tasks.acceptance: Tests invoking tp review or tp audit run against a relocated spec so engine.ReviewStateDir resolves outside the repository. --no-state is not used, because it disables the state under test.
source_sections: ### 6.1 Conditions on the suite as a whole
tasks.closed_reason:
- Tests emit against a relocated spec: relocatedSpec in internal/cli/testhelpers_test.go copies a repo spec plus any existing .tp-review/<base> into t.TempDir(), so engine.ReviewStateDir follows the spec out of the repository. Guard written first and observed RED against a deliberately wrong helper returning the repo path (both location assertions fired; the second named spec/.tp-review/0.36.0 as the directory that would have been written), then green. Measured beforehand: the existing suite already leaves spec/.tp-review/ and .tp/rounds/ byte-identical, so this closes the gap for the new tests that emit from the repository's real specs.
- --no-state is not used: it appears nowhere in the helper or the guard, and the doc comment records why. It disables review-state reads as well as writes, and that state is the subject (round number, skipped_roles, consecutive-clean count, whether regression is appended), so a suite run under it would pass while measuring a machine that had been switched off.
Gate green, four steps run separately: test -race 0, golangci-lint 0, deadcode 0, complexity 0.

tasks.title: Assert the suite mutates no state
tasks.acceptance: spec/.tp-review/ and .tp/rounds/ hash identically before and after a full go test ./... run. The check fails the build, and cannot be an ordinary test observing its own suite.

tasks.title: Test the suffix position
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: every emitted prompt with a non-empty output_path ends with the suffix, for tp review and for tp audit.

tasks.title: Test prompts with an empty output_path
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: no prompt whose output_path is empty ends with the suffix, over every --perspective value review.go validates plus --verify. The mode list is derived from the code, not written out.

tasks.title: Test the suffix appends once
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: the body minus its last 468 bytes neither ends with the suffix nor ends with a newline. This is the only assertion that fails on a double append or a missing strip.

tasks.title: Register the --role flag
tasks.acceptance: tp review and tp audit accept --role <name> as a single-valued string. It is not repeatable, and an empty value is treated as a name rather than as absent.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Both commands accept --role <name> as a single-valued string: registered in internal/cli/review.go and internal/cli/audit.go via Flags().StringVar, so pflag reports Value.Type() == string. TestRoleFlagIsRegisteredOnBothCommands asserts presence, type, empty default and usage text for review and audit; observed RED first on both subtests ('tp review must register --role', same for audit), then green.
- Not repeatable, and an empty value is a name rather than absent: StringVar takes one value, so a repeated occurrence overwrites instead of appending, and the guard pins the type against a StringArrayVar regression. The empty default is asserted, which is what lets a later task distinguish --role "" from an absent flag via Flags().Changed.
Three shipped guards fired in sequence the moment the flag existed, each one the mechanism working. TestNonGoals_NoCommandOrFlagIsAdded pins the command-and-flag surface, and its own comment fixes the procedure: a release that adds a flag updates the baseline in the same task and renames the constant to the tag it pins - so v034Surface became v036Surface with role on the review and audit lines, and the two failure messages stopped naming v0.34.2, which was about to become a stale claim on every future addition. TestSkillFlagInventoryIsComplete then required the flag in SKILL.md's inventory; two rows added, naming the three name classes rather than the flag alone, because the exit-0 case is the one an operator meets first and would otherwise read as a silent failure. That edit made SKILL.md plugin content that had changed, so TestPluginVersionIsBumpedWhenPluginContentChanges required the manifest bump to 0.36.0, and five session-start guards then failed until pluginMinVersion followed it - the preflight was correctly refusing a binary older than the plugin now demands. Gate green, four steps run separately: test -race 0, golangci-lint 0, deadcode 0, complexity 0.

tasks.acceptance: A name in the set the same invocation would emit without --role reduces prompts[] to that one byte-identical entry. Every other top-level key is unchanged except review_loop.instruction.

tasks.title: Refuse --role in non-emitting modes
tasks.acceptance: Per each command's own flag set, --role is accepted wherever prompts are emitted and exits 2 wherever none are. The refusal hint names both flags.

tasks.title: Test role selection fidelity
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: the selected entry is byte-identical to that role's entry in the unrestricted invocation, for tp review and tp audit.

tasks.title: Test the five skip reasons
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: each of §4.2.1's five reasons exits 0 on the command that can produce it, and an unrecognised name exits 2 with a distinguishable hint.

tasks.title: Test the per-command mode table
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: every legal mode emits one prompt and every refusing mode exits 2, run per command against that command's own list.

tasks.title: Test whole-panel equality
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: the per-role emissions concatenated in the unrestricted payload's own order equal that payload's prompts[], for both commands.

tasks.title: Pass --role in the unit brief
tasks.acceptance: tp resume's next_units[].brief_command for a role unit names that unit's own id. The change is made where the kind and the id are both in scope, since UnitKind.BriefCommand cannot see the id.

tasks.title: Narrow review_loop.instruction under --role
tasks.acceptance: Under --role the key is a sentence-subset of the unrestricted one, directing no action the single-prompt payload cannot support. Without --role it is byte-identical to before.

tasks.title: Test every unit brief runs
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: each unit's brief_command exits 0 in the phase that unit belongs to, under a fixture where a corpus role is skipped no-checklist-items.

tasks.title: Test regression stays unassigned
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: the emitted role set minus the unit set equals exactly the regression role, as set equality, at a round where regression emits.

tasks.title: Test the instruction narrowing
tasks.acceptance: Observed failing first: the --role instruction is a sentence-subset of the unrestricted one and carries none of its orchestrator directives; without the flag it is unchanged.

tasks.title: Run panel equality across every spec
tasks.acceptance: Whole-panel equality holds for every spec an unrestricted invocation emits prompts for, with the audit half given affected files via --affected-files or --base. A spec emitting nothing is named out of scope.

tasks.title: Document --role in the skill files
tasks.acceptance: skills/tp/SKILL.md and skills/tp/REFERENCE.md carry the flag, its three name classes, its per-command mode table. README.md's index lists it. Verified by running the documented commands.
